title: Quantification of Oculomotor Responses and Accommodation Through Instrumentation and Analysis Toolboxes
protocol: Check that the primary control monitor is indexed as 0 and that all successive monitors are indexed from 1 onwards.
Ensure proper spatial configuration of the stimulus monitors using Identify feature in Display settings.
Ensure the eye-tracking system is on the optical midline with a minimum camera distance of 38 cm.
Check that the autorefractor system is on the optical midline and positioned 1 m ± 0.05 m from the eyes.
Validate the configuration of the hardware and equipment by referencing the dimensions within Figure 1.
Ensure the desktop and corresponding eye-tracking hardware are configured and calibrated according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Establish BNC cable wiring from the desktop's analog outputs into the data acquisition (DAQ) board via an analog breakout terminal box (NI 2090A).
Identify the single-ended/differential (SE/DIFF) switch on the analog terminal breakout box reference switches, and set the switch to SE.
Identify the ground selection (RSE/NRSE) switch, and set the ground reference to referenced single-ended (RSE).
Perform the orientation of the autorefractor as per the manufacturer's recommendations.
Configure the autorefractor in direct alignment.
Perform manual operator-based triggering of the autorefractor to store the autorefractor recording data.
Ensure that an external removable storage device is utilized to save the autorefractor data.
Remove the external drive prior to starting the autorefractor software.
Reinsert the drive once the software is running.
Create a folder directory within the corresponding storage device for identifying participant profiles, session timings, and stimuli.
Begin the calibration of the autorefractor following software activation and insertion of an external storage device.
Monocularly occlude the left eye of the participant with an infrared transmission filter (IR Tx Filter).
Place a convex-sphere trial lens in front of the IR Tx filter.
Binocularly present a high acuity 4° stimulus from the physically near stimulus monitors.
Utilize the handheld trigger to progress once the participant reports the stimulus as visually single and clear.
Binocularly present a high acuity 16° stimulus from the physically near stimulus monitors.
Utilize the handheld trigger to progress once the participant reports the stimulus as visually single and clear.
Repeat these calibration procedures for each convex-sphere lens in diopters: −4, −3, −2, −1, +1, +2, +3, and +4.
Begin the calibration of the VisualEyes2020 stimulus display(s).
Open the virtual instrument (VI) file named Pix2Deg2020.vi.
Select the monitor to be calibrated by utilizing the stretch mode ID input field and the monitor's corresponding display index.
Select a stimulus image (e.g., RedLine.bmp) by typing the stimulus filename into the Line input field.
Run Pix2Deg2020.vi and adjust the stimulus position until it superimposes on a measured physical target.
Record the on-screen pixel value for the given degree value once alignment is achieved.
Repeat recording of calibration points with varying stimulated degree demands, ensuring at least three points are recorded.
Ensure VE2020 produces an output file named Cals.xls after recording each calibration point.
Utilize the calibration points in Cal.xls to apply a best-fit linear regression for mapping eye movement stimulus demands into pixels.
Define the VisualEyes display input file prior to the experiment.
Confirm the presence of four required tab-delimited parameters on the first row: stimulus timing (s); X-position (pixels); Y-position (pixels); and rotation (degrees).
Calculate the pixel value for each desired stimulus degree using the linear regression equation derived from calibration.
Confirm within the next row that the length (s) for which the stimulus is presented at its initial position and subsequent final position are present and tab-delimited.
Save the stimulus file in the directory as a VisualEyes input (VEI) file with an informative file name.
Repeat these procedures for each desired experimental stimulus.
Create a stimulus library for each stimulus monitor.
Name these libraries as dc_1.txt through dc_7.txt.
Validate the numerical ID for each stimulus monitor by clicking on Display > Screen Resolution > Identify.
Ensure that the device ID is the primary GPU (starting index 0).
Verify that left defines the left boundary of the screen (in pixels).
Define top as the top boundary of the screen (in pixels).
Specify width as the longitudinal width of the screen (in pixels).
Set height as the vertical height of the screen (in pixels).
Establish the stimulus number (Stim#) to associate with each stimulus file.
List various stimulus files that can be used within the experimental session.
Open a new text (.txt) file.
Utilize tab delimitation within the file.
End each line with two tab-delimited zeros.
Define initial time (s) and LED position values in the first row.
Define final time (s) and final LED position values in the second row.
Save the stimulus_name.vei file in the directory.
Repeat these steps for all stimuli.
Save all the stimulus files into the stimulus library, array_config.txt.
Ensure that the first row in array_config.txt is the communication (COM) port with default value COM1.
Specify the baud rate with default input value as 9600.
Indicate the data bit capacity with default input value as 8 bits.
Define the data parity index with default input value as 0.
Include stimulus file names of the flexible visual stimulator in succeeding rows.
Use the following general participant eligibility criteria: aged 18-35 years.
Ensure participants have 20/25 (or greater) corrected monocular visual acuity.
Verify stereo acuity of 500 s (or better) of arc in participants.
Confirm at least 2 weeks of utilizing proper refractive correction.
Use the following convergence insufficiency (CI) participant eligibility criteria: CISS score of 21 or greater.
Check failure of Sheard's criterion in participants.
Verify a near point of convergence (NPC) of 6 cm (or greater, at break).
Confirm 4Δ (or greater) exodeviation (near compared to far).
Use the following control participant eligibility criteria: CISS score less than 21.
Check less than 6Δ difference between near and far phoria.
Verify less than 6 cm (at break) NPC in participants.
Ensure passing of Sheard's criterion for controls.
Confirm sufficient minimum amplitude of accommodation as defined by Hofstetter's formula.
Use the following general participant ineligibility criteria: constant strabismus.
Exclude prior strabismus or refractive surgery from eligibility.
Do not include participants with dormant or manifested nystagmus.
Exclude encephalopathy and diseases impairing accommodative, vergence, or ocular motility.
Do not include 2Δ (or greater) vertical heterophoria in eligibility criteria.
Exclude inability to perform or comprehend study-related tests from participation.
The CI ineligibility criteria further includes participants with less than 5 diopters accommodative responses via Donder's push-up method.
Once informed consent is acquired, direct the participant to be seated in the haploscope.
Position the participant's forehead and chin against a fixed headrest.
Adjust the participant's chair height for neck comfort throughout the experiment duration.
Adjust eye movement recording cameras to capture the participant's eyes within the field of view.
Ask the participant to visually fixate on a presented target after proper seating in the haploscope and eye tracker/autorefractor.
Ensure visual targets are presented on the midsagittal plane by centering the participant's eyes.
Achieve eye centering with high acuity binocularly presented targets at the visual midline.
Adjust the eye-tracking gating and signal gains to capture anatomical features such as the limbus, pupil, and corneal reflection.
Validate the capture of eye movement data by asking the participant to perform repeated vergence and/or saccadic movements.
Open ReadScript.vi after preliminary validation and monitor calibration.
Select the experimental protocol script in the top-left corner of ReadScript.vi.
Press the white arrow in the top-left corner to run Acquire.vi via ReadScript.vi.
Provide the participant with a handheld trigger button and explain its use for data collection start.
Monitor Acquire.vi on the control monitor screen which plots recorded eye movement data in real-time.
When the experimental protocol is complete, ReadScript.vi automatically stops.
Generate and store data output files upon completion of the experiment.
Begin analysis by selecting the Preprocess Data button within VNEL eye movement analysis program (VEMAP).
Select one or many recorded data files from VE2020 for preprocessing in VEMAP.
Filter the selected data with a 20-order Butterworth filter: set to 40 Hz for vergence eye movements and 120 Hz or 250Hz for saccadic eye movements.
Store completed preprocessed data files within the VEMAP Preprocessed folder as .mat files.
Create a linear regression of the eye movement stimuli in degrees as a function of the recorded voltage values for left and right eye positions.
Use Pearson correlation coefficients and regression formulas to quantitatively assess the fitment.
Determine the monocular calibration gain from the slope of each regression.
Convert recorded (raw) voltages to degrees using the respective calibration gain.
Apply the determined gain consistently to each recorded eye movement stimulus section.
Perform the final step in the VEMAP processing dataflow.
Access the data analysis button within the VEMAP user interface (UI).
Preview and plot eye movements within a particular stimulus type and classification label as an ensemble plot.
Analyze subsets of eye movements via their classification labels using the Choose Classes button.
Holistically analyze eye movements without any applied classification filters.
Check that primary eye movement metrics correspond to each recorded eye movement, including latency, peak velocity, response amplitude, and final amplitude.
Inspect each eye movement response to ensure recorded metric validity.
Remeasure recorded metrics if they do not appear appropriate until valid values reflect each movement accurately.
Omit eye movements or reclassify their provided classification labels via the Reclassify button if the recorded metrics cannot adequately describe the recorded eye movement.
Export autorefractor data to an external storage device.
Transfer the exported data to a device with the Accommodative Movement Analysis Program (AMAP) installed.
Start the AMAP application.
Select either File Preprocessor or Batch Preprocessor in the AMAP.
Check the AMAP's progress bar and notifications.
Select a data directory using the file explorer window if preprocessing is not completed.
Generate folder directories from the AMAP's preprocessing for transparency and accessibility via the computer's local drive under AMAP_Output.
Load data into the current file directory using the Load Data button after preprocessing.
Select binocularly averaged data for the recorded accommodative refraction under the eye selector.
Switch the data type between accommodative refraction and oculomotor vergence via the Type Selector.
Check graphical customizations available for presenting data metrics.
Review Figure 10 for combinations of graphical options that can be selected.
Check default metrics for AMAP, including peak velocity (degrees/s), response amplitude (degrees), final amplitude (degrees), and others as specified.
Modify the response starting index through the metric modification spinners.
Adjust the response ending index using the metric modification spinners.
Change the peak velocity index via the metric modification spinners.
Analyze all recorded movements displayed.
Save analyzed metrics for each data file in the movement ID field or via navigation arrows.
Select the Save button to export analyzed data to a spreadsheet.
Perform manual classification (good/bad) for unanalyzed movements.
